trust_decision.summary: The generic PEG chat mapper decides which tool-call object later AST nodes write into (current_tool). At tool-close for an unnamed tool it destroys the pending optional but leaves current_tool pointing at the destroyed object, so later nodes write into freed string storage.

landing_point.why: The summary names common_chat_peg_mapper; map() is its only method that sets and uses current_tool.

fix_sites.entry_point: common_chat_parse() / common_chat_peg_parse() (common/chat.cpp:1447-1518), reached from server output parsing at tools/server/server-task.cpp:170 when the model's text is parsed for tool calls
fix_sites.module_kind: core library parser (common/), called by the HTTP server's chat-completions output path

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The gemma4 and minimax_m3 subclass mappers (common/chat-peg-parser.cpp:1057-1094, 1205-1232) build tool calls as locals and never use current_tool, so they are not a second implementation of the flaw.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No real out-of-scope route exists. The only nearby candidate is the reset in from_ast (common/chat-peg-parser.cpp:297), which a solver would rightly dismiss: nothing reads current_tool after that point.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unnamed or partial tool calls must still be discarded or flushed correctly during streaming; named tools must keep current_tool pointing at result.tool_calls.back() so later arg nodes append to the emitted call. Clearing current_tool too early (e.g. at line 370) would break argument accumulation.

O6_input_shapes: tool-close node for a tool whose tool-name was never seen (pending_tool_call still set), followed by further tool/arg nodes without a new tool-open

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The from_ast flush resets pending_tool_call without clearing current_tool. A planted post-flush step (e.g. an argument fix-up through args_target()) would reuse the dangling pointer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: from_ast already does post-processing after the visit (lines 300-312), so a maintainer could plausibly add argument normalisation there through the existing args_target() helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: current_tool points into the result.tool_calls vector. An added push_back to result.tool_calls before the next tool-open (e.g. auto-emitting a call at tool-id) would reallocate the vector and leave current_tool dangling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Lines 368-371 already push to the vector so streaming can see the call early; adding a similar early emit at another tag is a natural extension.

O9_family: memory-safety: use-after-free / dangling pointer to a destroyed std::optional payload (CWE-416)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C++17 compiler; the common/ library and tests build CPU-only
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test-chat-peg-parser.cpp and tests/test-chat-auto-parser.cpp construct common_chat_peg_mapper directly (e.g. tests/test-chat-peg-parser.cpp:378); behavioural tests can feed a hand-built PEG grammar and input under ASan without a model.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set current_tool = nullptr right after pending_tool_call.reset() at tool-close (the published one-liner); the over-broad version also clears it at line 370 and breaks arg accumulation for named tools.

out_of_scope_notes: common_chat_peg_parse partial-failure path (common/chat.cpp:1482-1500) runs the same mapper on lenient partial ASTs; this is the same route, not a new one.
unverified: Which concrete chat formats/grammars emit a tool-close without a tool-name, or tool/arg nodes after a close without a new tool-open, was not traced (common/parsers/, chat-auto-parser).
